title: FULL SILICON PROFILE — What Every Piece of northGate Contributes

cpu.node_atomic_role: ORCHESTRATOR — biomeOS runs here. Schedules GPU/NPU dispatch. Manages memory. Runs ollama serving. The CPU is the CONDUCTOR, not the instrument.
biomeOS_contribution: Runs biomeOS kernel (nucleus mode)
Manages 63 ollama model weights
Orchestrates GPU dispatch via neuralAPI
Handles all network I/O (LAN mesh)
Runs toadStool service discovery
Executes rustc compilation (gut acid)
3D V-Cache: 144MB L3 = entire models fit in cache for instant switching

memory.biomeOS_contribution: 32GB GDDR7 = 32 ollama models resident simultaneously. 1.8TB/s bandwidth = model blending in real-time. This is WHY northGate has 63 models — they FIT.

power.biomeOS_contribution: 575W = enough thermal budget for continuous inference + rendering + game physics simultaneously

clocks.biomeOS_contribution: 3.09GHz boost = individual thread operations complete in nanoseconds

cuda_cores.what_they_do: Massively parallel floating-point arithmetic. Each core does one multiply-add per clock.
cuda_cores.node_atomic_role: NEST — the engine room. Raw computation. Matrix multiplies for neural nets, physics simulations, shader execution.
biomeOS_contribution: ollama inference (all 63 models)
Game physics when Gaia plays
Scene tree traversal at massive parallelism
Rust compilation assist (GPU-accelerated linking future)
Model mixing/blending (llama_blend via neuralAPI)
cuda_cores.game_contribution: Every vertex, every pixel, every physics body. The 21,760 cores ARE the engine that renders games.

tensor_cores.what_they_do: Dedicated matrix multiply-accumulate units. 4×4 matrix ops in one clock cycle. FP8/FP16/INT8/INT4 precision.
tensor_cores.node_atomic_role: PROVER — the learning engine. Training, fine-tuning, inference acceleration. Tensor cores make AI FAST.
biomeOS_contribution: Accelerate ollama inference 4-10x over CUDA cores alone
Model training when Gaia learns from games
sweetGrass knowledge graph neural network training
sourDough fermentation depth — more tensor cores = deeper mastication
Pattern recognition in eaten game assets
llama_ask and llama_blend — tensor cores do the actual matrix math
tensor_cores.game_contribution: DLSS 4 frame generation, AI-upscaling, neural rendering. Tensor cores turn 1080p into 4K with AI.

rt_cores.what_they_do: Dedicated ray-triangle intersection + BVH traversal hardware. Each core tests millions of rays against geometry per second.
rt_cores.node_atomic_role: TOWER — the interface/signal layer. RT cores create VISUAL TRUTH. They trace light as it actually moves through a scene.
biomeOS_contribution: petalTongue real-time rendering for tube/plays/HUD
Scene tree visualization with physically-correct lighting
Game asset analysis — trace scene structure via BVH
Aperture simulation — RT cores literally model how light bends through a lens
Future: raytrace the organism itself — see data as light
rt_cores.game_contribution: Real-time ray tracing. Global illumination, reflections, shadows, caustics. The games look REAL because RT cores trace actual light paths.

nvenc.what_they_do: Hardware video encoding. Converts frames to compressed video at near-zero CPU cost.
biomeOS_contribution: RustDesk streaming from northGate to other gates
Record Gaia's gameplay for learning review
Stream to deckGate display in real-time
Encode gaiaU video classes (no CPU needed)
3 encoders = simultaneous multi-stream to multiple gates
nvenc.game_contribution: Record + stream gameplay simultaneously without performance impact.

nvdec.what_they_do: Hardware video decoding. Decompresses video at zero GPU compute cost.
biomeOS_contribution: Decode video feeds from other gates
Eat video game cinematics for learning
Process gaiaU class recordings

optical_flow.what_they_do: Dedicated motion estimation hardware. Analyzes pixel movement between frames.
biomeOS_contribution: DLSS frame generation (predicts future frames)
Scene change detection for Gaia's eyes
Game learning — detect what MOVED between frames

rasterizer.what_they_do: Raster Operations (ROPs) write pixels. Texture Mapping Units (TMUs) sample textures. The final stage of the rendering pipeline.
biomeOS_contribution: 192 ROPs = 192 pixels written per clock = 4K@240Hz native
680 TMUs = texture-rich scenes at maximum detail
petalTongue's WebGL CRT shader runs through these units

l2_cache.what_it_does: Shared cache between all GPU subsystems. Models, textures, intermediate results all live here.
l2_cache.biomeOS_contribution: 72MB L2 = multiple small ollama models fit entirely in GPU cache. Zero-latency switching between models.

ram.biomeOS_contribution: 96GB system RAM + 32GB VRAM = 128GB total. ALL 63 ollama models can be memory-mapped. CPU orchestrates, GPU infers, RAM stores everything.

storage.biomeOS_contribution: 5TB NVMe = entire Steam library fits. 1968GB of games + 2000GB for model weights + 1000GB for data. No spinning rust bottleneck.

nest.role: Engine + Rules — raw computation, game physics, model inference
nest.primal: nestGate equivalent — the engine room of the GPU

prover.role: Learning + Validation — training, inference acceleration, scene analysis
prover.primal: sweetGrass + squirrel equivalent — the learning/dispatch system

tower.role: Interface + Communication — rendering, encoding, display output
tower.primal: petalTongue + songBird equivalent — the visual/comms system

akida_akd1000.role_in_organism: FRACTAL ENUMERATOR — toadStool's edge. Classifies patterns at sub-milliwatt. The NPU doesn't compute — it RECOGNIZES.

rtx5090_tensor_cores.role_in_organism: BULK INFERENCE — tensor cores handle the heavy lifting. Many models, large batches, real-time.

npu_comparison.the_pattern: NPU = edge pattern recognition (0.001W, 18kHz). Tensor cores = bulk inference (200W, 838 TFLOPS). They COMPLEMENT — NPU identifies what to look at, tensor cores do the deep analysis. toadStool dispatches between them.

toadstool_as_fractal_enumerator.discovery: toadStool discovers ALL compute substrates: GPU, NPU, CPU, remote gates
toadstool_as_fractal_enumerator.fractal: The FractalRuntime adapts capabilities per deployment layer. A node knows what IT can do.
toadstool_as_fractal_enumerator.enumeration: toadStool enumerates the silicon tree like a scene tree — each subsystem is a node with capabilities
toadstool_as_fractal_enumerator.dispatch: Based on triads (granularity/refinement/focus), toadStool routes work to the right silicon
toadstool_as_fractal_enumerator.the_insight: toadStool IS the fractal enumerator. It walks the hardware tree, discovers what each node can do, and routes work based on capability — not hardcoded names. The NPU, GPU, and CPU are all just nodes in toadStool's scene tree.
